provisions.summary: Replaces the 2027 and 2029 bracket schedules (joint, head of household, single): repeals the scheduled 7.6%/7.9% and higher-bracket steps and sets the top rates at 8.25%, 9%, 10% and 11% with new thresholds. Modeled as two vintages (2027, 2029).

Child and dependent care credit: applicable percentage becomes an unspecified percentage, reduced 1 point per $3,000 of AGI above a blank threshold, floored at 15%. The percentage and threshold are blank, and the credit cannot be modeled.
provisions.quote: equal to per cent reduced by one percentage point for each $3,000, or fraction thereof, by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income exceeds $ ;

provisions.summary: Moves the repeal of the Act 261 (2019) tax credits (Part II, including the tax credit for research activities) up from January 1, 2030 to January 1, 2029.
provisions.quote: Part II shall take effect on [January 1, 2030.] January 1, 2029.

notes: (1) The bill takes effect July 1, 2050, which looks like a placeholder. Section 2 applies to tax years after Dec 31, 2026, and Part II takes effect Jan 1, 2029, so first_year is 2027. (2) Section 12 says the child and dependent care changes in section 2 are repealed on December 31, 2032 and the statute reverts to its pre-Act 163 form. That is after 2031. (3) The 2027 and 2029 bracket schedules are the unbracketed text. The bracketed 7.6%/7.9% schedules in those years are repealed. In the 2027 vintage the 7.6% band stays through $350,000 (joint), $262,500 (head of household) and $175,000 (single), and 8.25% starts above that. In 2029, 7.2% runs to the same thresholds. (4) The EITC and food/excise credits are not touched by the text; only the Act 163 sunset date is changed, and it is blank. Under rule 1 no credit keys are set, so current law (EITC reverts to 20% after 2027) stays in the model. (5) Tax credit for research activities is repealed through Act 261 (Section 10), so no section text for it is shown. (6) Capital gains, standard deduction and personal exemption are unchanged.
